Requirements:
Admission to the USC Herman Ostrow School of Dentistry of USC DDS program is highly competitive. Applicants are selected based on undergraduate academic performance, DAT scores, letters of recommendation, experiences and accomplishments (such as research, volunteer work, dental assisting and leadership), and a personal interview.
Important Note: The Ostrow School of Dentistry of USC participates in the Associated American Dental Schools Application Service (AADSAS). All application materials must be submitted through AADSAS. Once your application is verified by AADSAS, you will receive an email from USC with instructions to access our supplemental application. Please complete the supplemental application and return it along with a supplemental fee.
Academic Requirements
A bachelor’s degree from an accredited United States college or university is required. Official transcripts for all college work must be submitted to AADSAS.
You must have earned a minimum of 64 semester units (or 96 quarter units) from an accredited U.S. college or university. A minimum of 30 upper-division semester units are required.
A minimum GPA of 2.7 is required for regular admission.
Required courses:
Chemistry: Two semesters (8 units) of General Chemistry with labs and two semesters (8 units) of Organic Chemistry with labs.
Biology: Two semesters (8 units) of General Biology with labs.
Physics: Two semesters (8 units) of General Physics with labs.
English: Two semesters (6 units) of English (composition, literature or speech).
Biochemistry: One semester (3 units) of Biochemistry (lab not required, but recommended).
Microbiology: One semester (3 units) of Microbiology (lab not required, but recommended).
Anatomy/Physiology: One semester (3 units) of Anatomy or Physiology (lab not required, but recommended).
Immunology: One semester (3 units) of Immunology (lab not required, but recommended).
Psychology: One semester (3 units) of Psychology.
Statistics: One semester (3 units of Statistics.
All required science courses must be taken in person and completed at an accredited U.S. college or university. Online science courses are not accepted. The above courses must be completed with a grade of C or better. All required courses must be completed prior to matriculation. The admissions committee recommends applicants complete all required courses prior to applying.
Dental Admissions Test (DAT)
The DAT is required. All applicants must take the DAT within three years of the date of application. Scores must be submitted to AADSAS. For more information, visit the American Dental Association website.
Letters of Recommendation
Letters of recommendation must be submitted through AADSAS. We require one committee letter or three individual letters. If you opt for individual letters, one must be from a science professor and one from a non-science professor.
Experiences and Accomplishments
Applicants are encouraged to participate in extracurricular activities, volunteer opportunities, research, dental assisting and other work experiences.
Interviews
Interviews are by invitation only. Invited applicants will participate in multiple mini-interviews (MMI).
Program name: Doctor of Dental Surgery

Applicants applying for Fall 2024 must have taken the LSAT no earlier than June 2019. The Law School Admissions Council (LSAC) processes all JD applications. Applicants must register with the LSAC Credential Assembly Service (CAS), which provides an LSAT score and academic summary report to law schools. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended should be sent directly to LSAC. Applicants must also submit a personal statement, resume and letters of recommendation to LSAC.
